_about: v29.0 · episode 5 chapter 1 (e5c1), THE LOVE SPELL THAT FOLLOWED ME HOME: EVERY LINE IT SPEAKS, one row a line.

The source is docs/V29.0-E5C1-PLAN.md: its 10 (every line), its 8 and 9 (where each is said, and when), its 9.10 (the four lines under the cards) and its 11.6 (the two chants). Every line of Grandmaster Pho's goes to Chad before it is voiced (v26.0); until his word they stand as the plan drafts them (R3: build it all now, on the plan's defaults).
THIS FILE IS THE ONE COPY OF THE WORDS. masters/v29.0/assemble.py writes the chapter's SECS, LINES, SAID, CHANTS and WHO tables from it (src/chapters/e5/e5c1.js is generated: never edited by hand).

WHY IT IS HERE AND NOT YET IN src/voicelines.js: the registry takes a row only when its take is on disk (chaptertest: a planned row, `est`, is allowed only for a preview chapter, and Chad's rule of v27.0 is that no chapter is ever a preview). When a line is voiced: its take goes to assets/audio and assets/audio-opus under its key; `python3 -I masters/v29.0/script/registry.py --write` writes its row into src/voicelines.js (who: the `registry` name of its speaker below); its key goes into main.js's sound tables (and ADULT_TAKES for `zv`); and its MEASURED length goes here as `secs` (assemble.py then writes that instead of the provisional one).

A row: key (<speaker>51<id>: ph51 Grandmaster Pho, zv51 Master Zavier, gr51 Grace, mk51 Marcus); who (a speaker below); at (where in the chapter: open, room, keepsake, breaking, cord, home, night, barrier, endA to endD, dawn, card); where (the moment, in words); text (the words exactly as the plan has them). Optional: thought (his thought, heard as the man telling the story); same (another key with the same words); say (what the voice is given where it differs from the text); note; secs (its measured length, once voiced); chant with captions (a chant: its lines as [the Pali as chanted, its meaning], each a caption) and pace (its own provisional words a second).

PROVISIONAL LENGTHS: until `secs` is given, a line's length is its words / 2.3 seconds (the game's median pace; a chant at its own `pace`). Nothing is timed to these for good: a film built on them moves when the take is measured (v5.15).

HIS NAME IS WRITTEN Pho AND SAID Puu (Chad, R49 of episode 4 chapter 5): no line here says it aloud ('Grandmaster' is said in full), so none carries `say`; a line added that does must. A MASTER'S TITLE IS SPOKEN IN FULL (never 'LP'). ANUMODANA is said only by a monk: everyone here says thank you (v24.25).

THE TWO CHANTS (the plan's 11.6): their Pali and meaning VERBATIM from Thanissaro Bhikkhu's A Chanting Guide (dhammatalks.org), the page's own spelling and punctuation, its bold stress marks dropped. THE BREAKING: the guide carries the Discourse on Treasures as the Cha Ratana Paritta Gatha, 'The Six Protective Verses from the Discourse on Treasures' (Section0052), not the sutta's opening verses the plan names, so its first three verses are given here (the Buddha, the Dhamma, the concentration) and the change is said to the coordinator. THE BARRIER: the Jinapanjara's first four verses as docs/research/V29.0-LOVESPELL.md 3 has them (Section0093). Both go to Chad before they are voiced.

captions: Yaṅ-kiñci vittaṁ idha vā huraṁ vā / Saggesu vā yaṁ ratanaṁ paṇītaṁ / Na no samaṁ atthi Tathāgatena.
Whatever wealth in this world or the next, whatever exquisite treasure in the heavens, is not, for us, equal to the Tathāgata.
Idam-pi Buddhe ratanaṁ paṇītaṁ / Etena saccena suvatthi hotu.
This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Buddha. By this truth may there be well-being.
Khayaṁ virāgaṁ amataṁ paṇītaṁ / Yad-ajjhagā Sakyamunī samāhito / Na tena dhammena sam’atthi kiñci.
The exquisite deathless—dispassion, ending—discovered by the Sakyan Sage while in concentration: There is nothing equal to that Dhamma.
Idam-pi dhamme ratanaṁ paṇītaṁ / Etena saccena suvatthi hotu.
This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Dhamma. By this truth may there be well-being.
Yam-buddha-seṭṭho parivaṇṇayī suciṁ / Samādhim-ānantarik’aññam-āhu / Samādhinā tena samo na vijjati.
What the excellent Awakened One extolled as pure and called the concentration of unmediated knowing: No equal to that concentration can be found.
Idam-pi dhamme ratanaṁ paṇītaṁ / Etena saccena suvatthi hotu.
This, too, is an exquisite treasure in the Dhamma. By this truth may there be well-being.

captions: Jay'āsan'āgatā Buddhā / Jetvā Māraṁ savāhanaṁ / Catu-saccāsabhaṁ rasaṁ / Ye piviṅsu narāsabhā
The Buddhas, noble men who drank the nectar of the four noble truths, having come to the victory seat, having defeated Māra together with his mount:
Taṇhaṅkar'ādayo Buddhā / Aṭṭha-vīsati nāyakā / Sabbe patiṭṭhitā mayhaṁ / Matthake te munissarā.
These Buddhas—28 leaders, sovereign sages beginning with Taṇhaṅkara—are all established on the crown of my head.
Sīse patiṭṭhito mayhaṁ / Buddho dhammo dvilocane / Saṅgho patiṭṭhito mayhaṁ / Ure sabba-guṇākaro.
The Buddha is established in my head, the Dhamma in my two eyes, the Saṅgha—the mine of all virtues—is established in my chest.
Hadaye me Anuruddho / Sāriputto ca dakkhiṇe / Koṇḍañño piṭṭhi-bhāgasmiṁ / Moggallāno ca vāmake.
Anuruddha is in my heart, and Sārīputta on my right. Koṇḍañña is behind me, and Moggallāna on my left.
